content: Potassium tartrate, also known as dipotassium tartrate or argol, has the chemical formula K2C4H4O6. It is the potassium salt derived from tartaric acid. When dissolved in water, potassium tartrate undergoes a minor reaction, producing potassium hydroxide and tartaric acid. This compound is often mistaken for potassium bitartrate, but they are distinct substances. Potassium tartrate is a primary component of Weinstein, a crystalline or sandy residue that accumulates at the bottom of red wine bottles. This residue is typically found in higher-quality red wines made from grapes rich in minerals and that have not undergone chemical stabilization processes. In the context of food additives, potassium tartrate is assigned the E number E336.
